title.narrative: Output 1.4. Strengthened social dialogue and labour relations laws, processes and institutions

description.narrative:
TPB Bank PLC and Tanzania Union of Industrial and Commercial Workers (TUICO) signed a Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) in March 2020 to improve working conditions of workers in the commercial/ financial sector.
The tripartite constituents in Zanzibar - President’s Office Labour, Economic Affairs and Investment (POLEAI), Zanzibar Trade Union Congress (ZATUC) and Zanzibar Employers Association (ZANEMA) unanimously agreed on 14-15 October 2021 on a roadmap to reform some provisions of labour laws and practices with the aim to improve collective bargaining in Zanzibar. The roadmap is based on recommendations from a national study on assessment of the policies and legal frameworks on collective bargaining validated by the constituents when developing the roadmap. A Tripartite Steering Committee comprising 7 people was formed to oversee implementation of the Roadmap. The tripartite constituents in Mainland Tanzania – Prime Minister’s Office Labour, Youth, Employment and Persons with Disability (PMOLYED), Trade Union Congress of Tanzania (TUCTA) and Association of Tanzania Employers (ATE) unanimously agreed on 25-26 November 2021 on a roadmap to reform some provisions of labour laws and practices with the aim to improve collective bargaining in Mainland Tanzania. The roadmap is based on recommendations from a national study on assessment of the policies and legal frameworks on collective bargaining validated by the constituents when developing the roadmap. A Tripartite Steering Committee comprising 10 people was formed to oversee implementation of the Roadmap. Capacity building on collective bargaining was conducted for 40 representatives of the social partners in Mainland Tanzania (20) and Zanzibar (20) with the aim of enhancing skills for negotiators to be able to engage in collective bargaining and to conclude CBAs. With the support from Multi Partner Trust Fund (One UN fund); TZA/18/02/OUF, from January 2020, ILO delivered advisory services to the representatives of workers’ and employers’ organizations to help them design, negotiate and draft the CBA in accordance with the laws and international labour standards. Utilizing same resources; TZA/18/02/OUF, and in support of labour laws reform, ILO, in April, 2021, conducted a rapid assessment of the policy and legal frameworks in the United Republic of Tanzania. The consultant submitted a report with recommendations on, inter alia, making reforms on labour laws to ensure compliance with international labour standards and taking proper actions to address comments of the ILO supervisory bodies. An initial draft had been consulted with the constituents before finalizing the draft. The validation workshop in Zanzibar in October 2021 was funded by SIDA.

Output 1.4. Strengthened social dialogue and labour relations laws, processes and institutions

description.narrative:
The Capacity of the Commission for Mediation and Arbitration (CMA) & Dispute Handling Unit (DHU) was enhanced to mediate and arbitrate labour disputes by improving mediation and arbitration skills among mediators and arbitrators. This has improved dispute resolution in both Mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar. The success rate of mediated disputes has increased in both Mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar e.g. in 2020, the CMA (Mainland) registered 9,646 labour disputes, 8,366 of these disputes were successfully resolved. The success rate of disputes resolved is 87%. In Zanzibar, the DHU has improved service delivery in terms of resolving disputes where by in the year 2020, the DHU received 58 labour cases and managed to mediate 38 disputes, which is equivalent to 66%.
In March 2021, the Zanzibar Industrial Court Rules, 2021 were developed, validated and gazetted in the Government Gazette. Application of these Rules has effectively improved dispute resolution by the Court. Additionally, printing and dissemination of these Rules has increased awareness and improved compliance among the Court users and the social partners. In June 2021, the Labour Court Case Digests were developed, printed and 3,000 copies disseminated. The Digests cover decisions of the Court made in the years 2016, 2017 and 2018. Dissemination of jurisprudence has improved dispute resolution by the CMA and Labour Court. Arbitrators and Judges are able to decide cases in compliance with labour laws and international labour standards. Additionally, dissemination of jurisprudence has increased awareness and improved compliance among the social partners/ court users. With the support from One UN fund (TZA/18/02/OUF), ILO provided technical support from March 2020 to develop capacity of constituents on dispute prevention and resolution; 45 mediators and 40 arbitrators from the Commission for Mediation and Arbitration were trained to enhance their mediation and arbitration skills and legal procedures of handling arbitration. This included strengthening the capacity of dispute prevention and resolution institutions to resolve labour cases in compliance with labour laws. Further, the ILO contracted a consultant to conduct a rapid assessment of the policy and legal frameworks in the United Republic of Tanzania. The consultant has already submitted a report with recommendations on, inter alia, making reforms on labour laws to ensure compliance with international labour standards and taking proper action to address comments of the ILO supervisory bodies. Utilizing resources from One UN fund TZA/18/02/OUF, ILO supported the development and validation of the Zanzibar Industrial Court Rules, 2021, which were gazetted in March 2021 as well as the development and printing of the Labour Court Case Digests, which were disseminated in August 2021.

Output 1.3. Increased institutional capacity of labour administrations

description.narrative: The labour inspectorate under the Prime Minister’s Office – Labour, Youth, Employment and Persons with Disability (PMOLYED) developed a national Strategic Compliance Plan (SCP) in February 2021 in consultation with the Trade Union Congress of Tanzania (TUCTA) and Association of Tanzania Employers (ATE). The SCP targeted 24 enterprises in the construction sector and 16 enterprises in the transportation sector (total of 40 enterprises in both sectors). It was implemented in Dar es Salaam and Dodoma regions in Mainland Tanzania. The SCP includes a combined set of interventions such as obtaining relevant case information, initial inspection, follow-up action, inspection campaign and enforcement. The SCP respects the core elements of labour inspection as defined by Conventions No. 81 and No. 129. The SCP is also gender responsive. It addresses issues of non-discrimination, unionization of both female and male employees and equal treatment in terms of issuance of employment contracts. Implementation of the SCP will enable the labour inspectorate to improve its delivery. It is envisaged that in implementing the SCP labour inspectors will collaborate with other Ministry officials (such as IT and labour relations officers) and the social partners – ATE and TUCTA. This collaboration will help to improve compliance in the targeted sectors i.e. construction and transportation. The Strategic Compliance Plan in Tanzania is well underway with 53% (18/34) of actions devised in the plan implemented. This includes 70% of the enforcement intervention, 66% of the communication intervention and 11% of the education intervention. The capacity of 20 labour inspectors and 20 labour prosecutors was enhanced on implementation of the SCP and prosecution, respectively, to enable inspectors and prosecutors to implement their mandates. This has effectively improved compliance with labour laws. ILO provided technical assistance for capacity building of 20 labour inspectors and 20 labour prosecutors (40 in total) from the PMOLYED on strategic compliance planning and labour prosecution, respectively. Technical assistance was also provided for development and implementation of the Strategic Compliance Plan, including uploading relevant information in the SC Portal. Further support was provided for printing and dissemination of brochures for awareness raising.
